content: 1. Didanosine should be administered on an empty stomach, at least two hours before or at least four hours after rilpivirine, which must be taken with a meal. 2. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of disopyramide by prolonging the QTc interval. Close monitoring is required, and caution should be exercised. 3. Rilpivirine should be used cautiously when co-administered with drugs that have a known risk of Torsades de Pointes. 4. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of dofetilide by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 5. Dofetilide increases the toxicity of rilpivirine by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 6. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of dolasetron by prolonging the QTc interval. Close monitoring and caution are advised. 7. Donepezil and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Close monitoring and caution are required. 8. Doxepin and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Close monitoring and caution are required. 9. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of dronedarone by prolonging the QTc interval. Close monitoring and caution are advised. 10. Droperidol and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Close monitoring and caution are required. 11. Efavirenz decreases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 12. Efavirenz and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 13. Eliglustat and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Close monitoring and caution are required. 14. Elivaldogene autotemcel and rilpivirine may reduce each other’s effects. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Patients should not take antiretroviral medications for at least one month before initiating stem cell mobilization therapy and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 15. Rilpivirine should not be co-administered with elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF, as this combination is a complete HIV regimen. Co-administration is contraindicated. 16. Encorafenib and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 17. Entrectinib and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 18. Eribulin and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 19. Erythromycin base increases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, and rilpivirine increases erythromycin toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Close monitoring and caution are required. 20. Erythromycin ethylsuccinate increases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, and rilpivirine increases erythromycin toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Close monitoring and caution are required. 21. Erythromycin lactobionate increases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, and rilpivirine increases erythromycin toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Close monitoring and caution are required. 22. Erythromycin stearate increases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, and rilpivirine increases erythromycin toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Close monitoring and caution are required. 23. Escitalopram increases rilpivirine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval, and rilpivirine increases escitalopram toxicity by the same mechanism. Close monitoring and caution are required. 24. Eslicarbazepine acetate decreases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 25. Rilpivirine should not be co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inducers due to the potential for virologic failure and resistance to rilpivirine or the NNRTI class. 26. Esomeprazole decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. Co-administration is contraindicated, as it may lead to treatment failure and resistance. 27. Etravirine decreases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 28. Famotidine decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. Administer H2 antagonists at least 12 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine. Close monitoring and therapy modification are required. 29. Fexinidazole and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 30. Fingolimod and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Close monitoring and caution are required. 31. Rilpivirine increases flecainide toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Close monitoring and caution are advised. 32. Fluconazole increases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, and rilpivirine increases fluconazole toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Close monitoring and caution are required. 33. Fluoxetine and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Close monitoring and caution are required. 34. Fosamprenavir increases rilpivirine effects by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring and caution are required. 35. Rilpivirine increases foscarnet toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Close monitoring and caution are advised. 36. Fosphenytoin decreases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 37. Fostemsavir and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Close monitoring and caution are required. 38. Rilpivirine increases gemifloxacin toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Close monitoring and caution are advised. 39. Gepirone and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 40. Gilteritinib and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Close monitoring and caution are required. 41. Givinostat and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, obtain ECGs at baseline, during therapy, and as clinically indicated. Withhold therapy if QTc >500 ms or if there is a >60 ms change from baseline. 42. Granisetron and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Close monitoring and caution are required. 43. Rilpivirine increases haloperidol toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Close monitoring and caution are advised. 44. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 45. Hydroxyzine and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Close monitoring and caution are required. 46. Ibuprofen/famotidine decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. Administer famotidine at least 12 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine. Close monitoring and caution are required. 47. Ibutinide increases rilpivirine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval, and rilpivirine increases ibutinide toxicity by the same mechanism. Close monitoring and caution are required. 48. Iloperidone and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Close monitoring and caution are required. 49. Indapamide and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Close monitoring and caution are required. 50. Indinavir increases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring and caution are required. 51. Isoflurane and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 52. Isoniazid increases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring and caution are required. 53. Rilpivirine increases isradipine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Close monitoring and caution are advised. 54. Itraconazole increases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, and both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Close monitoring and caution are required. 55. Ketoconazole increases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring and caution are required. 56. Lansoprazole decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. Co-administration is contraindicated, as it may lead to treatment failure and resistance. 57. Rilpivirine increases lapatinib toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Close monitoring and caution are advised. 58. Lefamulin and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 59. Rilpivirine increases levofloxacin toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Close monitoring and caution are advised. 60. Levoketoconazole increases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring and caution are required. 61. Lithium and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Close monitoring and caution are required. 62. Lopinavir increases rilpivirine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, and rilpivirine increases lopinavir toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Close monitoring and caution are required. 63. Lovotibeglogene autotemcel and rilpivirine may interfere with each other. Discontinue antiretrovirals at least one month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 64. Rilpivirine increases lumefantrine toxicity by prolonging the QTc interval. Close monitoring and caution are advised. 65. Macimorelin and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 66. Magnesium chloride decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. Administer antacids at least 2 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 67. Magnesium gluconate decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. Administer antacids at least 2 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required.
